I will keep to the wheat-maize rotation on my land this year. In Quzhou County, that is still the most reliable way for me to use the full year, match the local climate, and protect my income. I am 65, so I do not want an overly complicated crop mix that demands too much hand labor or market timing. Because I am well educated, I trust measured input use and stable varieties more than gambling on novelty. So I will finish out the winter wheat that is already in the ground, manage water and fertilizer carefully through spring, harvest in early summer, and then plant summer maize immediately after. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because yield stability matters to me. I will control fertilizer rather than overapply it, irrigate wheat more often than maize because wheat is more exposed to spring drought here, and keep tillage practical: rotary tillage for wheat establishment and no-tillage or very light disturbance for maize after wheat harvest so I can save time and conserve moisture. I will also keep pesticide use moderate, only enough to protect yield and avoid obvious loss.
